question:
For what values of $k$ do the equations

$\begin{aligned} 2x + 3y + kz &= 0 \\ x + 2y + 2z &= 0 \\ 3x + 4y + 5z &= 0 \end{aligned}$

have a non-trivial solution?
explanation:
For non-trivial solution determinant must be zero.
Let $\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 3 & k \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \end{vmatrix}$

Expand along first row:
$= 2 \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 \end{vmatrix} - 3 \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 5 \end{vmatrix} + k \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{vmatrix}$

Calculate minors:
$\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 2 \times 5 - 2 \times 4 = 10 - 8 = 2$
$\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 1 \cdot 5 - 2 \cdot 3 = 5 - 6 = -1$
$\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = 1 \cdot 4 - 2 \cdot 3 = 4 - 6 = -2$

So,
$2 \cdot 2 - 3 \cdot (-1) + k \cdot (-2) = 0$
$4 + 3 - 2k = 0$
$7 - 2k = 0$
$k = \frac{7}{2}$

Thus, required value is $k = \frac{7}{2}$.
